A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SANER and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. Corresponding methods and experiments can be matched despite substantial reformatting and movement of material.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval-bias, ImageNet classification and image-generation experiments, plus loss and training-data-size ablations in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds generation-quality measurements, BLIP experiments and FACET evaluation in Appendix B.4-B.6.

M1.justification: The word-based neutralization, residual MLP, three loss components and inference rule are retained. v2 makes neutralized-text notation and original-text regularization more explicit in Sections 3.2-3.4 and Figure 2, but does not establish a changed procedure. The BLIP experiment introduces no documented algorithmic adaptation.

E1.justification: v2 adds gender-bias evaluation on FACET and generation-quality evaluation using COCO Karpathy test captions, extending the earlier occupational-prompt generation scenario. Existing coverage remains, while non-binary gender, additional FACET attributes and LLaVA are discussed only as potential extensions.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged: Original, Prompt and Projection for CLIP gender retrieval; Original and Projection for age/race retrieval and generation; Original and Prompt for classification. The new experiments reuse original-model and projection-based comparisons without introducing a new debiasing competitor.

E3.justification: New protocols include FID and CLIPScore evaluation on the COCO Karpathy test set and gender-bias evaluation using a model described as BLIP. The retained experiments preserve their stated training settings, retrieval metric and generation procedure, including 100 images per prompt. The new experiments provide limited configuration details.

E4.justification: Appendix B.4-B.6 substantially broadens supplementary validation: it tests preservation of generation fidelity and text alignment, transfer beyond CLIP, and robustness across another dataset distribution. The earlier loss and data-size ablations remain unchanged; the added explanation of contrastive-only regularization does not constitute a new ablation.

E5.justification: v1 Table 5 reports means and standard deviations across occupations for generation bias and gender-retention accuracy. Corresponding v2 Table 4 retains only means, removing this variability information. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed-based uncertainty or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds distinct result sets for generation quality, BLIP and FACET while retaining the original benchmark and ablation scores. Appendix B.4 reports original Stable Diffusion FID/CLIPScore of 28.1/31.2 versus SANER's 28.7/31.0. Table 10 reports SANER leading on all three FACET concept categories. Table 9 favors SANER over Projection in five of six BLIP comparisons, with the FairFace adjective exception being 15.3 versus 14.9. These are newly reported settings, not improvements over v1 under identical conditions.

T1.justification: Neither version supplies theoretical proofs or formal guarantees. The projection formula, debiasing objective and bias-metric definitions are retained. Explicit neutralization arguments in the revised notation add no new derivation or mathematical result.

C1.justification: The central claims of annotation-free debiasing, preservation of explicit attributes and improved bias mitigation remain. v2's abstract and contribution paragraph additionally emphasize avoiding CLIP retraining, access to its original training data, and retraining of downstream generation models. These foreground practical properties of the existing approach.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explanation for weaker contrastive-only regularization and discusses the effort, subjectivity and possible incompleteness of predefined attribute lists. Appendix F expands potential extensions to automated neutralization and LLaVA-like models. Earlier warnings about residual and unmeasured biases remain in Appendix G, although the separate main-text bias-metric limitations paragraph is removed.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly discloses a single 40 GB NVIDIA A100, approximately five hours of training, frozen non-debiasing modules, and dictionary-based grammatical substitutions. v2 also adds a project-page link; the PDFs alone do not establish its contents or code availability. Existing architecture dimensions, learning rate, batch size and loss weights are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting FACET, FID, CLIPScore, BLIP and the proposed LLaVA extension, while pruning several background citations. The experiment called BLIP cites the BLIP-2 reference. Positioning against adversarial and projection-based debiasing remains essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: Related Work moves from Section 2 to Section 7 and is shortened; insight summaries are consolidated, the conclusion is trimmed, and explanatory wording is refined. The main technical narrative remains largely intact. Appendix F adds a dedicated potential-extensions section.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document template, typography, headers and text-block layout throughout. Age and race results are combined into a compact main-text table, with complete tables moved to the appendix. The generation table is reformatted, Figure 2 gains explicit feature labels and a fuller caption, and new BLIP/FACET tables are added. Existing generated-image examples are retained and repositioned.

improvement.justification: Appendix B.4-B.6 supplies useful evidence about generation quality and model/dataset transfer that v1 lacked, while Appendix A improves implementation transparency. These gains are limited by sparse protocols for the new experiments and the removal of across-occupation standard deviations from the generation table. The new BLIP superiority statement also overlooks the FairFace adjective exception. Overall, the revision strengthens validation and documentation without substantially resolving the remaining evidential limitations.
